title: I built my research agent to say 'research only' more often than 'go'
author: Individual-Quote-958
selftext: Most AI trading tools want to hand you a signal. I went the other way. In Scout, a backtest has to pass validation before it counts, and if the checks fail the verdict is research only: interesting, not tradeable. Too few trades, missing bars, or an edge that dies once costs go in will all trigger it. Annoying at first. It has killed a lot of ideas that only looked good. Disclosure: I'm the founder. https://polarline.io

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
The research-only verdict is only as convincing as its thresholds, so I'd publish them: the minimum trade count, what counts as missing bars, and which costs go in (commission, spread, slippage per fill). The other question I'd expect here is out-of-sample: an edge that survives costs on the same data it was fitted on can still be overfit, so if Scout splits the history or runs walk-forward, say so. One idea it killed, shown with the check that failed, makes the point better than any description.
